note: Grand River floodplain wetland area near Meadville, a major waterfowl stop. The map marks ten primitive camping spots beside parking lots: this pin is the pair by the area headquarters on Blackhorn Drive; the best-equipped is the gravel loop with a privy on the shore of Jo Shelby Lake, reached from the north; the rest are small lots by the west-side pools and creeks. Refuge zones on the map are closed to all use October 15 to March 1, and some roads are impassable when wet or flooded. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'Camping: Individual Campsites'; brochure (2/2026) 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map', 14 days in 30; map (6/10/2025) 10 Primitive Camping symbols = GIS 229-232, 489-494, each by a lot. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. Pin (GIS 231 by HQ, beside lot 2269) fine; optional nudge onto the lot. Split proposed: Jo Shelby Lake camp (loop lot + privy on the lakeshore, 2.8 km NW, own road from the north), likely lakefront. Not waterfront kept for the HQ camp. Phone matches. Season (manual) left.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Individual Campsites'. Brochure (2/2026): 'Motor vehicles are restricted to gravel parking areas and gravel roadways unless roadways are posted closed. Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period... Groups of 10 campers or more must obtain a special use permit.' Map (Last Updated 6/10/2025) legend has Primitive Camping; ten symbols, each beside a Parking Lot symbol, matching GIS 229-232 and 489-494 (Type 'Primitive Camping Area'). Designated points beside lots: stays. No horse camp (the brochure mentions horses only on multi-use trails). Map road notes: Ames Road 'Impassable during flood', Belt Road 'Impassable when wet' (both north/east edges, not the HQ or Jo Shelby access). No 4WD/rig wording.

CAMPS (GIS -> map): HQ pair 231 (the pin) + 232, south of Blackhorn Dr by the Conservation Area Office, beside lots 2269/2268/2261, a privy at the road; 230 on Winnipeg Rd at Pool 1 (2.3 km NW); Jo Shelby Lake 229, 493, 494 along one gravel road with lots 1000, 999, 998 (2.3-3.2 km NNW); west side (Jeff Churan / Parsons Creek wetland complex) 489 by H1 off Acorn Rd (5.2 km), 491/492 by Pond 2 off Alton Rd and 490 by Pond 10 off Ames Rd (5.5-6.3 km). Imagery: 231 is at the edge of a tree clump on the gravel junction pad of lot 2269, with a larger open gravel area just SE; 232 is in woods 150 m N (its map symbol sits at the P). 489 (H1) is a small gravel turnaround in woods at a road end - a minor spot.
PIN: stored 39.69913,-93.30210 = GIS 231, at the tree edge beside lot 2269. Fine; optional nudge 20 m onto the lot at 39.69917,-93.30233.

SPLIT PROPOSED (one): 'Fountain Grove Conservation Area - Jo Shelby Lake' at lot 999 39.71850,-93.32297 (GIS 493 39.71814,-93.32307 is on open grass 40 m S). Imagery: a gravel loop lot ~45 m across with a privy, on a point of the Jo Shelby Lake shore; the map shows Parking, Privy, Primitive Camping, Disabled Accessible Parking and a Fishing Dock there, with two more camp points (229 S, 494 N) on the same road. 2.8 km from the HQ camp, reached from the north (Bolo Rd/Briar Dr side) rather than Blackhorn Dr; between them only an MDC service road. Nothing else in campgrounds.json within 3 km (near.py). Its own entry would be free/FCFS/no hookups like this one. WATERFRONT for the split: the loop's east edge is ~15-25 m from the water and GIS 493 sits on mown grass ~20 m from the shore with nothing between -> lakefront candidate (Jo Shelby Lake is several hectares, open water). The west-side camps are minor lots and not proposed.
WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept, for the HQ camp): no open water at 231/232; the managed pools to the south are seasonal wetland units behind levees.
PHONE: brochure '660/626-1794' (Fountain Grove CA) matches stored; also 'Chillicothe Office 660/646-6122'.

SEASON (manual, left): page 'Portions of this department area are closed to protect waterfowl from October 15 through March 1'; brochure 'Refuge Areas are in effect Oct. 15 through March 1 and are closed to all uses.' On the map the HQ camps lie in the Waterfowl Hunting Only Zone (single hatch), not the cross-hatched Refuge, so they stay open; the stored season.note is consistent.
